excerpts.text:
[Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy") was the host nation of the [2026 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Winter_Olympics "2026 Winter Olympics") in [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan") and [Cortina d'Ampezzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cortina_d'Ampezzo "Cortina d'Ampezzo"), from 6 to 22 February 2026.

Italy ended the 2026 Winter Olympics by winning 10 gold, 6 silver and 14 bronze medals, setting a new record in number of medals won (20 medals was the previous record, reached in [Lillehammer 1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Winter_Olympics "1994 Winter Olympics")).[[2]](#cite_note-2) This new record comes 5 years after the new record in summer olympics set in [Tokyo 2020 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics "2020 Summer Olympics") (that were held in 2021) and equalled in [Paris 2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics"). Moreover Italy won more gold and bronze medals than in any other [winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy_at_the_Winter_Olympics "Italy at the Winter Olympics") (the previous records being 7 and 8, respectively), and clinched at least one medal in ten different sports.

On 18 February, short-track speed skater [Arianna Fontana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arianna_Fontana "Arianna Fontana") won her third medal at these Olympics and her fourteenth overall, becoming Italy's [record medal-winning athlete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy_at_the_Olympics#Athletes_with_most_medals "Italy at the Olympics") of all time (previous record was held by Italian fencer [Edoardo Mangiarotti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edoardo_Mangiarotti "Edoardo Mangiarotti"), with 13 medals).[[3]](#cite_note-3)

🇮🇹 Italy has made history at the 2026 Winter Olympics 🥇❄️ 
 
With a record-breaking 30 medals — including 10 gold, 6 silver, and 14 bronze — this is Italy’s strongest performance at a Winter Games ever, surpassing their previous record of 20 medals in 1994. 
 
Italian athletes also won medals in 10 different sports, proving the country’s growing strength and versatility across winter disciplines.
